summary: Independent review of the updated Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 60d03f00beace6be3ec5f94bf95c506c3333c25070ac717f341bebd32e9067a4. All 27 packaged files byte-match source. Month headings now recognize engineer-authored comment, note, and report labels and a trailing dash at end of line. Explicit older/previous/earlier/undated/original note headings create separate internal blocks, preventing their text from being assigned to the preceding month. Public monthly sections retain exact rendered offsets, and merge replacements remain confined to changed monthly ranges; undated raw content stays outside them. Calendar-date and narrative rejection remain covered. Independently executed all 13 focused parser/comment-view tests successfully. No blocking issues found. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment.
caveats: Heading recognition remains heuristic. Heading-like standalone prose may create a section, and yearless headings still use the epic reference year and existing cross-year confirmation safeguards.
Undated text combines the introduction and explicitly undated blocks for presentation. It remains undated context, not evidence that it belongs to the displayed review month.
Parser expansion changes interpretation of existing source text without rewriting it. Explicit later saves retain the existing canonical month-heading behavior for the edited month.

Existing AI grounding/temporal limitations, usage completeness, SDK cache/cancellation, popup accessibility/scroll, refresh concurrency, journal growth, revision conflicts, non-atomic updates, preference semantics, host/catalog/history limits, and AllUsers sharing caveats remain.
Current GUS Apps host metadata still relies on verified-definition snapshots; automatic detection of future list-column changes remains unavailable without live list-view REST capability.

This review combined static source/artifact inspection with 13 independently executed focused tests. The implementing agent reported all 142 Node tests and fetch/reload plus monthly-AI browser checks passed. Those full suites, actual GUS historical replay, production-host/model behavior, remote publication, and golden-tag movement were not independently verified.
